chunks: And with the former chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, that Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said:

When you are determined to do something good, then do not delay it. For indeed Allah, blessed and exalted be He, may look upon His servant while he is engaged in an act of obedience to Him, and He says: By My Might and My Majesty, I will never punish you after this.

And when you are inclined to commit a sin, then do not do it, for indeed Allah, blessed and exalted be He, may look upon the servant while he is engaged in an act of disobedience, and He says: By My Might and My Majesty, I will never forgive you.

key_terms.تبارك وتعالى: Blessed and Exalted be He; formulaic praise of Allah expressing His transcendence and blessedness
key_terms.طاعته: His obedience; acts of worship and compliance with divine commandments
key_terms.عزتي وجلالي: My Might and My Majesty; a divine oath formula indicating the utmost solemnity and certainty of God's decree
key_terms.معاصيه: His acts of disobedience; sins and transgressions against divine law
key_terms.هممت: Intend or resolve firmly; implies a decisive internal commitment, not a passing thought

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about hastening to do good and avoiding sin?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) conveys a powerful teaching about the decisive nature of human intention and divine response. The hadith reveals that a single moment of virtuous resolve can earn eternal divine protection from punishment, while a moment of sinful intent can seal one's fate. This narration, transmitted through the highly reliable chain of Ali ibn Mahziyar and Ibn Abi Umayr, was addressed to the early Shia community to emphasize the urgency of moral action and the gravity of divine oaths sworn by God's own Might and Majesty.
